facts.text: Bohannon sits just 7 feet above sea level, making it one of the lowest points in Mathews County and a frontline against rising tides.
The community’s name honors the Bohannon family, whose 1667 land patent on the East River helped shape the area’s early tobacco economy.
Bohannon’s historic core includes the 1900 Ro-Mar Market, a vernacular commercial building that once served as the town’s social hub.
The Peninsula School, built around 1920 in Classical Revival style, later became a community center, reflecting early 20th‑century educational priorities.
The East River borders Bohannon to the east, while Mill Creek outlines its southern and western edges, weaving the community into Mathews County’s tidal network.
Bohannon experiences a humid subtropical climate, with July highs near 87°F and annual rainfall around 47 inches, supporting lush maritime forests and tidal wetlands.
